purpose: Prospectively test whether a calibration-only stochastic transmission extension can recover a known synthetic conditional edge-transmission probability while preserving the F1a scheduler and v0.1.1 cognitive-state boundaries.

estimand.name: q_transmit
estimand.mathematical_role: Conditional Bernoulli probability of realised transmission on one declared eligible directed edge given a realised Share.
estimand.numerator: realised endogenous recipient ExposureEvents generated by the recovery-only policy

expected_relations: mean exposure proportion increases with q_transmit
larger opportunity count improves recovery precision without changing q_transmit
abstract delay changes event timing but not expected full-horizon exposure proportion
sensitivity_scope.rationale: The first recovery design has one stochastic process parameter and two controlled design factors; a bounded grid plus explicit stress conditions is sufficient for this prospective stage.

observability_boundary: The benchmark observes realised Share-edge opportunities and realised recipient exposures directly from synthetic provenance.
This does not establish that equivalent quantities are observable in any human or platform dataset.
If future empirical data do not observe the denominator and numerator separately, q_transmit may not be identifiable under this estimator.
interpretation_boundary: A passing result is a best-case synthetic identifiability result, not evidence that the stochastic transmission mechanism is true.
No parameter value in this design is a population, platform, social-network, or human estimate.
RECOVERY_TESTED would remain below EMPIRICALLY_CONSTRAINED and ACTIVE on the Issue #110 validation ladder.
No full endogenous Share-to-Share feedback loop or formal System Dynamics classification is implied.

method_basis.role: prospective parameter recovery using simulated data with known generating parameters
structured parameter estimation and sensitivity analysis for simulation models
bounded sensitivity analysis starting point for limited-complexity agent-based models
